name: articular cartilage
cue: thin layer of cartilage covering an epiphysis; reduces friction and acts as a shock absorber

name: articulation
cue: where two bone surfaces meet

name: bone
cue: hard, dense connective tissue that forms the structural elements of the skeleton

cue: (singular = canaliculus) channels within the bone matrix that house one of an osteocyte’s many cytoplasmic extensions that it uses to communicate and receive nutrients

cue: semi-rigid connective tissue found on the skeleton in areas where flexibility and smooth surfaces support movement

cue: longitudinal channel in the center of each osteon; contains blood vessels, nerves, and lymphatic vessels; also known as the Haversian canal

name: closed reduction
cue: manual manipulation of a broken bone to set it into its natural position without surgery

name: compact bone
cue: dense osseous tissue that can withstand compressive forces

name: diaphysis
cue: tubular shaft that runs between the proximal and distal ends of a long bone

name: diploë
cue: layer of spongy bone, that is sandwiched between the two layers of compact bone found in flat bones

name: endochondral ossification
cue: process in which bone forms by replacing hyaline cartilage

name: endosteum
cue: delicate membranous lining of a bone’s medullary cavity

name: epiphyseal line
cue: completely ossified remnant of the epiphyseal plate

name: epiphyseal plate
cue: (also, growth plate) sheet of hyaline cartilage in the metaphysis of an immature bone; replaced by bone tissue as the organ grows in length

name: epiphysis
cue: wide section at each end of a long bone; filled with spongy bone and red marrow

cue: collar of hyaline cartilage and bone that forms around the outside of a fracture

name: flat bone
cue: thin and curved bone; serves as a point of attachment for muscles and protects internal organs

name: fracture
cue: broken bone

name: fracture hematoma
cue: blood clot that forms at the site of a broken bone

name: hematopoiesis
cue: production of blood cells, which occurs in the red marrow of the bones

name: hole
cue: opening or depression in a bone

name: hypercalcemia
cue: condition characterized by abnormally high levels of calcium

name: hypocalcemia
cue: condition characterized by abnormally low levels of calcium

name: internal callus
cue: fibrocartilaginous matrix, in the endosteal region, between the two ends of a broken bone

name: intramembranous ossification
cue: process by which bone forms directly from mesenchymal tissue

name: irregular bone
cue: bone of complex shape; protects internal organs from compressive forces

name: lacunae
cue: (singular = lacuna) spaces in a bone that house an osteocyte

name: long bone
cue: cylinder-shaped bone that is longer than it is wide; functions as a lever

name: medullary cavity
cue: hollow region of the diaphysis; filled with yellow marrow

name: modeling
cue: process, during bone growth, by which bone is resorbed on one surface of a bone and deposited on another

cue: small opening in the middle of the external surface of the diaphysis, through which an artery enters the bone to provide nourishment

name: open reduction
cue: surgical exposure of a bone to reset a fracture

name: orthopedist
cue: doctor who specializes in diagnosing and treating musculoskeletal disorders and injuries

name: osseous tissue
cue: bone tissue; a hard, dense connective tissue that forms the structural elements of the skeleton

name: ossification
cue: (also, osteogenesis) bone formation

name: ossification center
cue: cluster of osteoblasts found in the early stages of intramembranous ossification

name: osteoblast
cue: cell responsible for forming new bone

name: osteoclast
cue: cell responsible for resorbing bone

name: osteocyte
cue: primary cell in mature bone; responsible for maintaining the matrix

name: osteogenic cell
cue: undifferentiated cell with high mitotic activity; the only bone cells that divide; they differentiate and develop into osteoblasts

name: osteoid
cue: uncalcified bone matrix secreted by osteoblasts

name: osteon
cue: (also, Haversian system) basic structural unit of compact bone; made of concentric layers of calcified matrix

cue: disease characterized by a decrease in bone mass; occurs when the rate of bone resorption exceeds the rate of bone formation, a common occurrence as the body ages

name: perforating canal
cue: (also, Volkmann’s canal) channel that branches off from the central canal and houses vessels and nerves that extend to the periosteum and endosteum

name: perichondrium
cue: membrane that covers cartilage

name: periosteum
cue: fibrous membrane covering the outer surface of bone and continuous with ligaments

name: primary ossification center
cue: region, deep in the periosteal collar, where bone development starts during endochondral ossification

name: projection
cue: bone markings where part of the surface sticks out above the rest of the surface, where tendons and ligaments attach

name: proliferative zone
cue: region of the epiphyseal plate that makes new chondrocytes to replace those that die at the diaphyseal end of the plate and contributes to longitudinal growth of the epiphyseal plate

name: red marrow
cue: connective tissue in the interior cavity of a bone where hematopoiesis takes place

name: remodeling
cue: process by which osteoclasts resorb old or damaged bone at the same time as and on the same surface where osteoblasts form new bone to replace that which is resorbed

name: reserve zone
cue: region of the epiphyseal plate that anchors the plate to the osseous tissue of the epiphysis

name: secondary ossification center
cue: region of bone development in the epiphyses

name: sesamoid bone
cue: small, round bone embedded in a tendon; protects the tendon from compressive forces

name: short bone
cue: cube-shaped bone that is approximately equal in length, width, and thickness; provides limited motion

name: skeletal system
cue: organ system composed of bones and cartilage that provides for movement, support, and protection

name: spongy bone
cue: (also, cancellous bone) trabeculated osseous tissue that supports shifts in weight distribution

name: trabeculae
cue: (singular = trabecula) spikes or sections of the lattice-like matrix in spongy bone

name: yellow marrow
cue: connective tissue in the interior cavity of a bone where fat is stored

name: zone of calcified matrix
cue: region of the epiphyseal plate closest to the diaphyseal end; functions to connect the epiphyseal plate to the diaphysis

name: zone of maturation and hypertrophy
cue: region of the epiphyseal plate where chondrocytes from the proliferative zone grow and mature and contribute to the longitudinal growth of the epiphyseal plate

cue: upper border of mandibular body that contains the lower teeth

name: alveolar process of the maxilla
cue: curved, inferior margin of the maxilla that supports and anchors the upper teeth

name: angle of the mandible
cue: rounded corner located at outside margin of the body and ramus junction

name: angle of the rib
cue: portion of rib with greatest curvature; together, the rib angles form the most posterior extent of the thoracic cage

cue: anterior portion of the ring-like C1 (atlas) vertebra

cue: ligament that runs the length of the vertebral column, uniting the anterior aspects of the vertebral bodies

name: anulus fibrosus
cue: tough, fibrous outer portion of an intervertebral disc, which is strongly anchored to the bodies of the adjacent vertebrae

cue: all bones of the upper and lower limbs, plus the girdle bones that attach each limb to the axial skeleton

name: articular tubercle
cue: smooth ridge located on the inferior skull, immediately anterior to the mandibular fossa

name: atlas
cue: first cervical (C1) vertebra

name: axial skeleton
cue: central, vertical axis of the body, including the skull, vertebral column, and thoracic cage

name: axis
cue: second cervical (C2) vertebra

name: body of the rib
cue: shaft portion of a rib

cue: portion of the skull that contains and protects the brain, consisting of the eight bones that form the cranial base and rounded upper skull

name: calvaria
cue: (also, skullcap) rounded top of the skull

cue: zig-zag tunnel providing passage through the base of the skull for the internal carotid artery to the brain; begins anteromedial to the styloid process and terminates in the middle cranial cavity, near the posterior-lateral base of the sella turcica

name: cervical curve
cue: posteriorly concave curvature of the cervical vertebral column region; a secondary curve of the vertebral column

name: cervical vertebrae
cue: seven vertebrae numbered as C1–C7 that are located in the neck region of the vertebral column

name: clavicular notch
cue: paired notches located on the superior-lateral sides of the sternal manubrium, for articulation with the clavicle

name: condylar process of the mandible
cue: thickened upward projection from posterior margin of mandibular ramus

name: condyle
cue: oval-shaped process located at the top of the condylar process of the mandible

name: coronal suture
cue: joint that unites the frontal bone to the right and left parietal bones across the top of the skull

name: coronoid process of the mandible
cue: flattened upward projection from the anterior margin of the mandibular ramus

cue: hyaline cartilage structure attached to the anterior end of each rib that provides for either direct or indirect attachment of most ribs to the sternum

cue: site on the lateral sides of a thoracic vertebra for articulation with the head of a rib

name: costal groove
cue: shallow groove along the inferior margin of a rib that provides passage for blood vessels and a nerve

name: cranial cavity
cue: interior space of the skull that houses the brain

name: cranium
cue: skull

cue: bony projection (odontoid process) that extends upward from the body of the C2 (axis) vertebra

name: ear ossicles
cue: three small bones located in the middle ear cavity that serve to transmit sound vibrations to the inner ear

cue: one of several small, air-filled spaces located within the lateral sides of the ethmoid bone, between the orbit and upper nasal cavity

cue: unpaired bone that forms the roof and upper, lateral walls of the nasal cavity, portions of the floor of the anterior cranial fossa and medial wall of orbit, and the upper portion of the nasal septum

name: external acoustic meatus
cue: ear canal opening located on the lateral side of the skull

name: external occipital protuberance
cue: small bump located at the midline on the posterior skull

name: facet
cue: small, flattened area on a bone for an articulation (joint) with another bone, or for muscle attachment

name: facial bones
cue: fourteen bones that support the facial structures and form the upper and lower jaws and the hard palate

cue: vertebrochondral ribs 8–12 whose costal cartilage either attaches indirectly to the sternum via the costal cartilage of the next higher rib or does not attach to the sternum at all

cue: vertebral ribs 11–12 that do not attach to the sternum or to the costal cartilage of another rib

cue: expanded area of fibrous connective tissue that separates the brain case bones of the skull prior to birth and during the first year after birth

name: foramen lacerum
cue: irregular opening in the base of the skull, located inferior to the exit of carotid canal

name: foramen magnum
cue: large opening in the occipital bone of the skull through which the spinal cord emerges and the vertebral arteries enter the cranium

name: foramen ovale of the middle cranial fossa
cue: oval- shaped opening in the floor of the middle cranial fossa

cue: round opening in the floor of the middle cranial fossa, located between the superior orbital fissure and foramen ovale

cue: small opening in the floor of the middle cranial fossa, located lateral to the foramen ovale

cue: unpaired bone that forms forehead, roof of orbit, and floor of anterior cranial fossa

name: frontal sinus
cue: air-filled space within the frontal bone; most anterior of the paranasal sinuses

name: glabella
cue: slight depression of frontal bone, located at the midline between the eyebrows

name: greater wings of sphenoid bone
cue: lateral projections of the sphenoid bone that form the anterior wall of the middle cranial fossa and an area of the lateral skull

cue: bony structure that forms the roof of the mouth and floor of the nasal cavity, formed by the palatine process of the maxillary bones and the horizontal plate of the palatine bones

name: head of the rib
cue: posterior end of a rib that articulates with the bodies of thoracic vertebrae

cue: medial extension from the palatine bone that forms the posterior quarter of the hard palate

name: hyoid bone
cue: small, U-shaped bone located in upper neck that does not contact any other bone

cue: paired openings that pass anteriorly from the anterior-lateral margins of the foramen magnum deep to the occipital condyles

cue: shallow depression on top of the sella turcica that houses the pituitary (hypophyseal) gland

name: inferior articular process
cue: bony process that extends downward from the vertebral arch of a vertebra that articulates with the superior articular process of the next lower vertebra

name: inferior nasal concha
cue: one of the paired bones that project from the lateral walls of the nasal cavity to form the largest and most inferior of the nasal conchae

name: infraorbital foramen
cue: opening located on anterior skull, below the orbit

name: internal acoustic meatus
cue: opening into petrous ridge, located on the lateral wall of the posterior cranial fossa

cue: structure located between the bodies of adjacent vertebrae that strongly joins the vertebrae; provides padding, weight bearing ability, and enables vertebral column movements

cue: opening located between adjacent vertebrae for exit of a spinal nerve

name: jugular (suprasternal) notch
cue: shallow notch located on superior surface of sternal manubrium

name: jugular foramen
cue: irregularly shaped opening located in the lateral floor of the posterior cranial cavity

name: kyphosis
cue: (also, humpback or hunchback) excessive posterior curvature of the thoracic vertebral column region

name: lacrimal bone
cue: paired bones that contribute to the anterior-medial wall of each orbit

name: lacrimal fossa
cue: shallow depression in the anterior- medial wall of the orbit, formed by the lacrimal bone that gives rise to the nasolacrimal canal

cue: inverted V-shaped joint that unites the occipital bone to the right and left parietal bones on the posterior skull

name: lamina
cue: portion of the vertebral arch on each vertebra that extends between the transverse and spinous process

cue: lateral extensions of the sphenoid bone that form the bony lip separating the anterior and middle cranial fossae

name: ligamentum flavum
cue: series of short ligaments that unite the lamina of adjacent vertebrae

name: lingula
cue: small flap of bone located on the inner (medial) surface of mandibular ramus, next to the mandibular foramen

name: lordosis
cue: (also, swayback) excessive anterior curvature of the lumbar vertebral column region

name: lumbar curve
cue: posteriorly concave curvature of the lumbar vertebral column region; a secondary curve of the vertebral column

name: lumbar vertebrae
cue: five vertebrae numbered as L1–L5 that are located in lumbar region (lower back) of the vertebral column

name: mandible
cue: unpaired bone that forms the lower jaw bone; the only moveable bone of the skull

name: mandibular foramen
cue: opening located on the inner (medial) surface of the mandibular ramus

name: mandibular fossa
cue: oval depression located on the inferior surface of the skull

name: mandibular notch
cue: large U-shaped notch located between the condylar process and coronoid process of the mandible

name: manubrium
cue: expanded, superior portion of the sternum

name: mastoid process
cue: large bony prominence on the inferior, lateral skull, just behind the earlobe

name: maxillary bone
cue: (also, maxilla) paired bones that form the upper jaw and anterior portion of the hard palate

name: maxillary sinus
cue: air-filled space located with each maxillary bone; largest of the paranasal sinuses

name: medial pterygoid plate
cue: paired, flattened bony projections of the sphenoid bone located on the inferior skull medial to the lateral pterygoid plate; form the posterior portion of the nasal cavity lateral wall

name: median sacral crest
cue: irregular ridge running down the midline of the posterior sacrum that was formed from the fusion of the spinous processes of the five sacral vertebrae

name: mental foramen
cue: opening located on the anterior- lateral side of the mandibular body

name: mental protuberance
cue: inferior margin of anterior mandible that forms the chin

name: middle cranial fossa
cue: centrally located cranial fossa that extends from the lesser wings of the sphenoid bone to the petrous ridge

name: middle nasal concha
cue: nasal concha formed by the ethmoid bone that is located between the superior and inferior conchae

name: mylohyoid line
cue: bony ridge located along the inner (medial) surface of the mandibular body

name: nasal bone
cue: paired bones that form the base of the nose

name: nasal cavity
cue: opening through skull for passage of air

name: nasal conchae
cue: curved bony plates that project from the lateral walls of the nasal cavity; include the superior and middle nasal conchae, which are parts of the ethmoid bone, and the independent inferior nasal conchae bone

cue: flat, midline structure that divides the nasal cavity into halves, formed by the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone, vomer bone, and septal cartilage

name: neck of the rib
cue: narrowed region of a rib, next to the rib head

name: notochord
cue: rod-like structure along dorsal side of the early embryo; largely disappears during later development but does contribute to formation of the intervertebral discs

cue: expanded portion of the supraspinous ligament within the posterior neck; interconnects the spinous processes of the cervical vertebrae and attaches to the base of the skull

cue: gel-like central region of an intervertebral disc; provides for padding, weight- bearing, and movement between adjacent vertebrae

name: occipital bone
cue: unpaired bone that forms the posterior portions of the brain case and base of the skull

name: occipital condyle
cue: paired, oval-shaped bony knobs located on the inferior skull, to either side of the foramen magnum

name: optic canal
cue: opening spanning between middle cranial fossa and posterior orbit

name: orbit
cue: bony socket that contains the eyeball and associated muscles

name: palatine bone
cue: paired bones that form the posterior quarter of the hard palate and a small area in floor of the orbit

name: palatine process
cue: medial projection from the maxilla bone that forms the anterior three quarters of the hard palate

cue: cavities within the skull that are connected to the conchae that serve to warm and humidify incoming air, produce mucus, and lighten the weight of the skull; consist of frontal, maxillary, sphenoidal, and ethmoidal sinuses

name: parietal bone
cue: paired bones that form the upper, lateral sides of the skull

name: pedicle
cue: portion of the vertebral arch that extends from the vertebral body to the transverse process

name: perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone
cue: downward, midline extension of the ethmoid bone that forms the superior portion of the nasal septum

name: petrous ridge
cue: petrous portion of the temporal bone that forms a large, triangular ridge in the floor of the cranial cavity, separating the middle and posterior cranial fossae; houses the middle and inner ear structures

name: posterior (dorsal) sacral foramen
cue: one of the series of paired openings located on the posterior (dorsal) side of the sacrum

name: posterior arch
cue: posterior portion of the ring-like C1 (atlas) vertebra

name: posterior cranial fossa
cue: deepest and most posterior cranial fossa; extends from the petrous ridge to the occipital bone

name: posterior longitudinal ligament
cue: ligament that runs the length of the vertebral column, uniting the posterior sides of the vertebral bodies

name: primary curve
cue: anteriorly concave curvatures of the thoracic and sacrococcygeal regions that are retained from the original fetal curvature of the vertebral column

name: pterion
cue: H-shaped suture junction region that unites the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bones on the lateral side of the skull

name: ramus of the mandible
cue: vertical portion of the mandible

name: ribs
cue: thin, curved bones of the chest wall

name: sacral canal
cue: bony tunnel that runs through the sacrum

name: sacral foramina
cue: series of paired openings for nerve exit located on both the anterior (ventral) and posterior (dorsal) aspects of the sacrum

name: sacral hiatus
cue: inferior opening and termination of the sacral canal

name: sacral promontory
cue: anterior lip of the base (superior end) of the sacrum

name: sacrococcygeal curve
cue: anteriorly concave curvature formed by the sacrum and coccyx; a primary curve of the vertebral column

name: sacrum
cue: single bone located near the inferior end of the adult vertebral column that is formed by the fusion of five sacral vertebrae; forms the posterior portion of the pelvis

name: sagittal suture
cue: joint that unites the right and left parietal bones at the midline along the top of the skull

name: sclerotome
cue: medial portion of a somite consisting of mesenchyme tissue that will give rise to bone, cartilage, and fibrous connective tissues

name: scoliosis
cue: abnormal lateral curvature of the vertebral column

name: secondary curve
cue: posteriorly concave curvatures of the cervical and lumbar regions of the vertebral column that develop after the time of birth

name: sella turcica
cue: elevated area of sphenoid bone located at midline of the middle cranial fossa

name: septal cartilage
cue: flat cartilage structure that forms the anterior portion of the nasal septum

name: skeleton
cue: bones of the body

name: skull
cue: bony structure that forms the head, face, and jaws, and protects the brain; consists of 22 bones

name: somite
cue: one of the paired, repeating blocks of tissue located on either side of the notochord in the early embryo

name: sphenoid bone
cue: unpaired bone that forms the central base of skull

name: sphenoid sinus
cue: air-filled space located within the sphenoid bone; most posterior of the paranasal sinuses

name: spinous process
cue: unpaired bony process that extends posteriorly from the vertebral arch of a vertebra

name: squamous suture
cue: joint that unites the parietal bone to the squamous portion of the temporal bone on the lateral side of the skull

cue: junction line between manubrium and body of the sternum and the site for attachment of the second rib to the sternum

name: sternum
cue: flattened bone located at the center of the anterior chest

name: styloid process
cue: downward projecting, elongated bony process located on the inferior aspect of the skull

name: stylomastoid foramen
cue: opening located on inferior skull, between the styloid process and mastoid process

cue: bony process that extends upward from the vertebral arch of a vertebra that articulates with the inferior articular process of the next higher vertebra

cue: paired processes that extend upward from the sacrum to articulate (join) with the inferior articular processes from the L5 vertebra

name: superior nasal concha
cue: smallest and most superiorly located of the nasal conchae; formed by the ethmoid bone

cue: paired bony lines on the posterior skull that extend laterally from the external occipital protuberance

name: superior orbital fissure
cue: irregularly shaped opening between the middle cranial fossa and the posterior orbit

name: supraorbital foramen
cue: opening located on anterior skull, at the superior margin of the orbit

name: supraorbital margin
cue: superior margin of the orbit

name: supraspinous ligament
cue: ligament that interconnects the spinous processes of the thoracic and lumbar vertebrae

name: suture
cue: junction line at which adjacent bones of the skull are united by fibrous connective tissue

name: temporal bone
cue: paired bones that form the lateral, inferior portions of the skull, with squamous, mastoid, and petrous portions

name: temporal fossa
cue: shallow space on the lateral side of the skull, above the level of the zygomatic arch

name: temporal process of the zygomatic bone
cue: short extension from the zygomatic bone that forms the anterior portion of the zygomatic arch

name: thoracic cage
cue: consists of 12 pairs of ribs and sternum

name: thoracic curve
cue: anteriorly concave curvature of the thoracic vertebral column region; a primary curve of the vertebral column

name: thoracic vertebrae
cue: twelve vertebrae numbered as T1–T12 that are located in the thoracic region (upper back) of the vertebral column

name: transverse foramen
cue: opening found only in the transverse processes of cervical vertebrae

name: transverse process
cue: paired bony processes that extends laterally from the vertebral arch of a vertebra

name: true ribs
cue: vertebrosternal ribs 1–7 that attach via their costal cartilage directly to the sternum

name: tubercle of the rib
cue: small bump on the posterior side of a rib for articulation with the transverse process of a thoracic vertebra

name: vertebra
cue: individual bone in the neck and back regions of the vertebral column

name: vertebral (spinal) canal
cue: bony passageway within the vertebral column for the spinal cord that is formed by the series of individual vertebral foramina

name: vertebral arch
cue: bony arch formed by the posterior portion of each vertebra that surrounds and protects the spinal cord

name: vertebral column
cue: entire sequence of bones that extend from the skull to the tailbone

cue: opening associated with each vertebra defined by the vertebral arch that provides passage for the spinal cord

name: vomer bone
cue: unpaired bone that forms the inferior and posterior portions of the nasal septum

name: xiphoid process
cue: small process that forms the inferior tip of the sternum

cue: elongated, free-standing arch on the lateral skull, formed anteriorly by the temporal process of the zygomatic bone and posteriorly by the zygomatic process of the temporal bone

name: zygomatic bone
cue: cheekbone; paired bones that contribute to the lateral orbit and anterior zygomatic arch

name: zygomatic process of the temporal bone
cue: extension from the temporal bone that forms the posterior portion of the zygomatic arch

cue: large, cup-shaped cavity located on the lateral side of the hip bone; formed by the junction of the ilium, pubis, and ischium portions of the hip bone

name: acromial end of the clavicle

name: acromial process
cue: acromion of the scapula

cue: articulation between the acromion of the scapula and the acromial end of the clavicle

name: acromion
cue: flattened bony process that extends laterally from the scapular spine to form the bony tip of the shoulder

cue: small, bony bump located on the superior aspect of the medial epicondyle of the femur

name: anatomical neck
cue: line on the humerus located around the outside margin of the humeral head

name: ankle joint
cue: joint that separates the leg and foot portions of the lower limb; formed by the articulations between the talus bone of the foot inferiorly, and the distal end of the tibia, medial malleolus of the tibia, and lateral malleolus of the fibula superiorly

cue: small, bony projection located on the anterior margin of the ilium, below the anterior superior iliac spine

name: anterior sacroiliac ligament
cue: strong ligament between the sacrum and the ilium portions of the hip bone that supports the anterior side of the sacroiliac joint

name: anterior superior iliac spine
cue: rounded, anterior end of the iliac crest

cue: enlarged ridge of ectoderm at the distal end of a limb bud that stimulates growth and elongation of the limb

name: arcuate line of the ilium
cue: smooth ridge located at the inferior margin of the iliac fossa; forms the lateral portion of the pelvic brim

name: arm
cue: region of the upper limb located between the shoulder and elbow joints; contains the humerus bone

name: auricular surface of the ilium
cue: roughened area located on the posterior, medial side of the ilium of the hip bone; articulates with the auricular surface of the sacrum to form the sacroiliac joint

name: base of the metatarsal bone
cue: expanded, proximal end of each metatarsal bone

name: bicipital groove
cue: intertubercular groove; narrow groove located between the greater and lesser tubercles of the humerus

name: calcaneus
cue: heel bone; posterior, inferior tarsal bone that forms the heel of the foot

name: capitulum
cue: knob-like bony structure located anteriorly on the lateral, distal end of the humerus

cue: one of the eight small bones that form the wrist and base of the hand; these are grouped as a proximal row consisting of (from lateral to medial) the scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, and pisiform bones, and a distal row containing (from lateral to medial) the trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, and hamate bones

cue: passageway between the anterior forearm and hand formed by the carpal bones and flexor retinaculum

cue: articulation between one of the carpal bones in the distal row and a metacarpal bone of the hand

cue: collarbone; elongated bone that articulates with the manubrium of the sternum medially and the acromion of the scapula laterally

name: coracoid process
cue: short, hook-like process that projects anteriorly and laterally from the superior margin of the scapula

name: coronoid fossa

name: coronoid process of the ulna

name: costoclavicular ligament
cue: band of connective tissue that unites the medial clavicle with the first rib

name: coxal bone
cue: hip bone

name: cuboid
cue: tarsal bone that articulates posteriorly with the calcaneus bone, medially with the lateral cuneiform bone, and anteriorly with the fourth and fifth metatarsal bones

name: deltoid tuberosity
cue: roughened, V-shaped region located laterally on the mid-shaft of the humerus

name: distal radioulnar joint
cue: articulation between the head of the ulna and the ulnar notch of the radius

name: distal tibiofibular joint
cue: articulation between the distal fibula and the fibular notch of the tibia

name: elbow joint
cue: joint located between the upper arm and forearm regions of the upper limb; formed by the articulations between the trochlea of the humerus and the trochlear notch of the ulna, and the capitulum of the humerus and the head of the radius

name: femur
cue: thigh bone; the single bone of the thigh

name: fibula
cue: thin, non-weight-bearing bone found on the lateral side of the leg

name: fibular notch
cue: wide groove on the lateral side of the distal tibia for articulation with the fibula at the distal tibiofibular joint

name: flexor retinaculum
cue: strong band of connective tissue at the anterior wrist that spans the top of the U- shaped grouping of the carpal bones to form the roof of the carpal tunnel

name: foot
cue: portion of the lower limb located distal to the ankle joint

name: forearm
cue: region of the upper limb located between the elbow and wrist joints; contains the radius and ulna bones

name: fossa
cue: (plural = fossae) shallow depression on the surface of a bone

name: fovea capitis
cue: minor indentation on the head of the femur that serves as the site of attachment for the ligament to the head of the femur

name: glenohumeral joint
cue: shoulder joint; formed by the articulation between the glenoid cavity of the scapula and the head of the humerus

name: glenoid cavity
cue: (also, glenoid fossa) shallow depression located on the lateral scapula, between the superior and lateral borders

name: gluteal tuberosity
cue: roughened area on the posterior side of the proximal femur, extending inferiorly from the base of the greater trochanter

name: greater pelvis
cue: (also, greater pelvic cavity or false pelvis) broad space above the pelvic brim defined laterally by the fan-like portion of the upper ilium

name: greater sciatic foramen
cue: pelvic opening formed by the greater sciatic notch of the hip bone, the sacrum, and the sacrospinous ligament

name: greater sciatic notch
cue: large, U-shaped indentation located on the posterior margin of the ilium, superior to the ischial spine

name: greater trochanter
cue: large, bony expansion of the femur that projects superiorly from the base of the femoral neck

name: greater tubercle
cue: enlarged prominence located on the lateral side of the proximal humerus

name: hallux
cue: big toe; digit 1 of the foot

name: hamate
cue: from the lateral side, the fourth of the four distal carpal bones; articulates with the lunate and triquetrum proximally, the fourth and fifth metacarpals distally, and the capitate laterally

name: hand
cue: region of the upper limb distal to the wrist joint

name: head of the femur
cue: rounded, proximal end of the femur that articulates with the acetabulum of the hip bone to form the hip joint

name: head of the fibula
cue: small, knob-like, proximal end of the fibula; articulates with the inferior aspect of the lateral condyle of the tibia

name: head of the humerus
cue: smooth, rounded region on the medial side of the proximal humerus; articulates with the glenoid fossa of the scapula to form the glenohumeral (shoulder) joint

name: head of the metatarsal bone
cue: expanded, distal end of each metatarsal bone

name: head of the radius
cue: disc-shaped structure that forms the proximal end of the radius; articulates with the capitulum of the humerus as part of the elbow joint, and with the radial notch of the ulna as part of the proximal radioulnar joint

name: head of the ulna
cue: small, rounded distal end of the ulna; articulates with the ulnar notch of the distal radius, forming the distal radioulnar joint

name: hip bone
cue: coxal bone; single bone that forms the pelvic girdle; consists of three areas, the ilium, ischium, and pubis

name: hip joint
cue: joint located at the proximal end of the lower limb; formed by the articulation between the acetabulum of the hip bone and the head of the femur

name: hook of the hamate bone
cue: bony extension located on the anterior side of the hamate carpal bone

name: humerus
cue: single bone of the upper arm

name: iliac crest
cue: curved, superior margin of the ilium

name: iliac fossa
cue: shallow depression found on the anterior and medial surfaces of the upper ilium

name: ilium
cue: superior portion of the hip bone

name: inferior angle of the scapula
cue: inferior corner of the scapula located where the medial and lateral borders meet

name: inferior pubic ramus
cue: narrow segment of bone that passes inferiorly and laterally from the pubic body; joins with the ischial ramus to form the ischiopubic ramus

name: infraglenoid tubercle
cue: small bump or roughened area located on the lateral border of the scapula, near the inferior margin of the glenoid cavity

name: infraspinous fossa
cue: broad depression located on the posterior scapula, inferior to the spine

name: intercondylar eminence
cue: irregular elevation on the superior end of the tibia, between the articulating surfaces of the medial and lateral condyles

name: intercondylar fossa
cue: deep depression on the posterior side of the distal femur that separates the medial and lateral condyles

name: intermediate cuneiform
cue: middle of the three cuneiform tarsal bones; articulates posteriorly with the navicular bone, medially with the medial cuneiform bone, laterally with the lateral cuneiform bone, and anteriorly with the second metatarsal bone

name: interosseous border of the fibula
cue: small ridge running down the medial side of the fibular shaft; for attachment of the interosseous membrane between the fibula and tibia

name: interosseous border of the radius
cue: narrow ridge located on the medial side of the radial shaft; for attachment of the interosseous membrane between the ulna and radius bones

name: interosseous border of the tibia
cue: small ridge running down the lateral side of the tibial shaft; for attachment of the interosseous membrane between the tibia and fibula

name: interosseous border of the ulna
cue: narrow ridge located on the lateral side of the ulnar shaft; for attachment of the interosseous membrane between the ulna and radius

name: interosseous membrane of the forearm
cue: sheet of dense connective tissue that unites the radius and ulna bones

name: interosseous membrane of the leg
cue: sheet of dense connective tissue that unites the shafts of the tibia and fibula bones

name: interphalangeal joint
cue: articulation between adjacent phalanx bones of the hand or foot digits

name: intertrochanteric crest
cue: short, prominent ridge running between the greater and lesser trochanters on the posterior side of the proximal femur

name: intertrochanteric line
cue: small ridge running between the greater and lesser trochanters on the anterior side of the proximal femur

name: intertubercular groove (sulcus)
cue: bicipital groove; narrow groove located between the greater and lesser tubercles of the humerus

name: ischial ramus
cue: bony extension projecting anteriorly and superiorly from the ischial tuberosity; joins with the inferior pubic ramus to form the ischiopubic ramus

name: ischial spine
cue: pointed, bony projection from the posterior margin of the ischium that separates the greater sciatic notch and lesser sciatic notch

name: ischial tuberosity
cue: large, roughened protuberance that forms the posteroinferior portion of the hip bone; weight-bearing region of the pelvis when sitting

name: ischiopubic ramus
cue: narrow extension of bone that connects the ischial tuberosity to the pubic body; formed by the junction of the ischial ramus and inferior pubic ramus

name: ischium
cue: posteroinferior portion of the hip bone

name: knee joint
cue: joint that separates the thigh and leg portions of the lower limb; formed by the articulations between the medial and lateral condyles of the femur, and the medial and lateral condyles of the tibia

name: lateral border of the scapula
cue: diagonally oriented lateral margin of the scapula

name: lateral condyle of the femur
cue: smooth, articulating surface that forms the distal and posterior sides of the lateral expansion of the distal femur

name: lateral condyle of the tibia
cue: lateral, expanded region of the proximal tibia that includes the smooth surface that articulates with the lateral condyle of the femur as part of the knee joint

name: lateral cuneiform
cue: most lateral of the three cuneiform tarsal bones; articulates posteriorly with the navicular bone, medially with the intermediate cuneiform bone, laterally with the cuboid bone, and anteriorly with the third metatarsal bone

name: lateral epicondyle of the femur
cue: roughened area of the femur located on the lateral side of the lateral condyle

name: lateral epicondyle of the humerus
cue: small projection located on the lateral side of the distal humerus

name: lateral malleolus
cue: expanded distal end of the fibula

name: lateral supracondylar ridge
cue: narrow, bony ridge located along the lateral side of the distal humerus, superior to the lateral epicondyle

name: leg
cue: portion of the lower limb located between the knee and ankle joints

name: lesser pelvis
cue: (also, lesser pelvic cavity or true pelvis) narrow space located within the pelvis, defined superiorly by the pelvic brim (pelvic inlet) and inferiorly by the pelvic outlet

name: lesser sciatic foramen
cue: pelvic opening formed by the lesser sciatic notch of the hip bone, the sacrospinous ligament, and the sacrotuberous ligament

name: lesser sciatic notch
cue: shallow indentation along the posterior margin of the ischium, inferior to the ischial spine

name: lesser trochanter
cue: small, bony projection on the medial side of the proximal femur, at the base of the femoral neck

name: lesser tubercle
cue: small, bony prominence located on anterior side of the proximal humerus

name: ligament of the head of the femur
cue: ligament that spans the acetabulum of the hip bone and the fovea capitis of the femoral head

name: limb bud
cue: small elevation that appears on the lateral side of the embryo during the fourth or fifth week of development, which gives rise to an upper or lower limb

name: linea aspera
cue: longitudinally running bony ridge located in the middle third of the posterior femur

name: lunate
cue: from the lateral side, the second of the four proximal carpal bones; articulates with the radius proximally, the capitate and hamate distally, the scaphoid laterally, and the triquetrum medially

name: medial border of the scapula
cue: elongated, medial margin of the scapula

name: medial condyle of the femur
cue: smooth, articulating surface that forms the distal and posterior sides of the medial expansion of the distal femur

name: medial condyle of the tibia
cue: medial, expanded region of the proximal tibia that includes the smooth surface that articulates with the medial condyle of the femur as part of the knee joint

name: medial cuneiform
cue: most medial of the three cuneiform tarsal bones; articulates posteriorly with the navicular bone, laterally with the intermediate cuneiform bone, and anteriorly with the first and second metatarsal bones

name: medial epicondyle of the femur
cue: roughened area of the distal femur located on the medial side of the medial condyle

name: medial epicondyle of the humerus
cue: enlarged projection located on the medial side of the distal humerus

name: medial malleolus
cue: bony expansion located on the medial side of the distal tibia

name: metacarpal bone
cue: one of the five long bones that form the palm of the hand; numbered 1–5, starting on the lateral (thumb) side of the hand

name: metacarpophalangeal joint
cue: articulation between the distal end of a metacarpal bone of the hand and a proximal phalanx bone of the thumb or a finger

name: metatarsal bone
cue: one of the five elongated bones that forms the anterior half of the foot; numbered 1–5, starting on the medial side of the foot

name: metatarsophalangeal joint
cue: articulation between a metatarsal bone of the foot and the proximal phalanx bone of a toe

name: midcarpal joint
cue: articulation between the proximal and distal rows of the carpal bones; contributes to movements of the hand at the wrist

name: navicular
cue: tarsal bone that articulates posteriorly with the talus bone, laterally with the cuboid bone, and anteriorly with the medial, intermediate, and lateral cuneiform bones

name: neck of the femur
cue: narrowed region located inferior to the head of the femur

name: neck of the radius
cue: narrowed region immediately distal to the head of the radius

name: obturator foramen
cue: large opening located in the anterior hip bone, between the pubis and ischium regions

name: olecranon fossa
cue: large depression located on the posterior side of the distal humerus; this space receives the olecranon process of the ulna when the elbow is fully extended

name: olecranon process
cue: expanded posterior and superior portions of the proximal ulna; forms the bony tip of the elbow

name: patella
cue: kneecap; the largest sesamoid bone of the body; articulates with the distal femur

name: patellar surface
cue: smooth groove located on the anterior side of the distal femur, between the medial and lateral condyles; site of articulation for the patella

name: pectineal line
cue: narrow ridge located on the superior surface of the superior pubic ramus

name: pectoral girdle
cue: shoulder girdle; the set of bones, consisting of the scapula and clavicle, which attaches each upper limb to the axial skeleton

name: pelvic brim
cue: pelvic inlet; the dividing line between the greater and lesser pelvic regions; formed by the superior margin of the pubic symphysis, the pectineal lines of each pubis, the arcuate lines of each ilium, and the sacral promontory

name: pelvic girdle
cue: hip girdle; consists of a single hip bone, which attaches a lower limb to the sacrum of the axial skeleton

name: pelvic inlet
cue: pelvic brim

name: pelvic outlet
cue: inferior opening of the lesser pelvis; formed by the inferior margin of the pubic symphysis, right and left ischiopubic rami and sacrotuberous ligaments, and the tip of the coccyx

name: pelvis
cue: ring of bone consisting of the right and left hip bones, the sacrum, and the coccyx

name: phalanx bone of the foot
cue: (plural = phalanges) one of the 14 bones that form the toes; these include the proximal and distal phalanges of the big toe, and the proximal, middle, and distal phalanx bones of toes two through five

name: phalanx bone of the hand
cue: (plural = phalanges) one of the 14 bones that form the thumb and fingers; these include the proximal and distal phalanges of the thumb, and the proximal, middle, and distal phalanx bones of the fingers two through five

name: pisiform
cue: from the lateral side, the fourth of the four proximal carpal bones; articulates with the anterior surface of the triquetrum

name: pollex
cue: (also, thumb) digit 1 of the hand

name: posterior inferior iliac spine
cue: small, bony projection located at the inferior margin of the auricular surface on the posterior ilium

name: posterior sacroiliac ligament
cue: strong ligament spanning the sacrum and ilium of the hip bone that supports the posterior side of the sacroiliac joint

name: posterior superior iliac spine
cue: rounded, posterior end of the iliac crest

name: proximal radioulnar joint
cue: articulation formed by the radial notch of the ulna and the head of the radius

name: proximal tibiofibular joint
cue: articulation between the head of the fibula and the inferior aspect of the lateral condyle of the tibia

name: pubic arch
cue: bony structure formed by the pubic symphysis, and the bodies and inferior pubic rami of the right and left pubic bones

name: pubic body
cue: enlarged, medial portion of the pubis region of the hip bone

name: pubic symphysis
cue: joint formed by the articulation between the pubic bodies of the right and left hip bones

name: pubic tubercle
cue: small bump located on the superior aspect of the pubic body

name: pubis
cue: anterior portion of the hip bone

name: radial fossa
cue: small depression located on the anterior humerus above the capitulum; this space receives the head of the radius when the elbow is maximally flexed

name: radial notch of the ulna
cue: small, smooth area on the lateral side of the proximal ulna; articulates with the head of the radius as part of the proximal radioulnar joint

name: radial tuberosity
cue: oval-shaped, roughened protuberance located on the medial side of the proximal radius

name: radiocarpal joint
cue: wrist joint, located between the forearm and hand regions of the upper limb; articulation formed proximally by the distal end of the radius and the fibrocartilaginous pad that unites the distal radius and ulna bone, and distally by the scaphoid, lunate, and triquetrum carpal bones

name: radius
cue: bone located on the lateral side of the forearm

name: sacroiliac joint
cue: joint formed by the articulation between the auricular surfaces of the sacrum and ilium

name: sacrospinous ligament
cue: ligament that spans the sacrum to the ischial spine of the hip bone

name: sacrotuberous ligament
cue: ligament that spans the sacrum to the ischial tuberosity of the hip bone

name: scaphoid
cue: from the lateral side, the first of the four proximal carpal bones; articulates with the radius proximally, the trapezoid, trapezium, and capitate distally, and the lunate medially

name: scapula
cue: shoulder blade bone located on the posterior side of the shoulder

name: shaft of the femur
cue: cylindrically shaped region that forms the central portion of the femur

name: shaft of the fibula
cue: elongated, slender portion located between the expanded ends of the fibula

name: shaft of the humerus
cue: narrow, elongated, central region of the humerus

name: shaft of the radius
cue: narrow, elongated, central region of the radius

name: shaft of the tibia
cue: triangular-shaped, central portion of the tibia

name: shaft of the ulna
cue: narrow, elongated, central region of the ulna

name: soleal line
cue: small, diagonally running ridge located on the posterior side of the proximal tibia

name: spine of the scapula
cue: prominent ridge passing mediolaterally across the upper portion of the posterior scapular surface

name: sternal end of the clavicle
cue: medial end of the clavicle that articulates with the manubrium of the sternum

name: sternoclavicular joint
cue: articulation between the manubrium of the sternum and the sternal end of the clavicle; forms the only bony attachment between the pectoral girdle of the upper limb and the axial skeleton

name: styloid process of the radius
cue: pointed projection located on the lateral end of the distal radius

name: styloid process of the ulna
cue: short, bony projection located on the medial end of the distal ulna

name: subpubic angle
cue: inverted V-shape formed by the convergence of the right and left ischiopubic rami; this angle is greater than 80 degrees in females and less than 70 degrees in males

name: subscapular fossa
cue: broad depression located on the anterior (deep) surface of the scapula

name: superior angle of the scapula
cue: corner of the scapula between the superior and medial borders of the scapula

name: superior border of the scapula
cue: superior margin of the scapula

name: superior pubic ramus
cue: narrow segment of bone that passes laterally from the pubic body to join the ilium

name: supraglenoid tubercle
cue: small bump located at the superior margin of the glenoid cavity

name: suprascapular notch
cue: small notch located along the superior border of the scapula, medial to the coracoid process

name: supraspinous fossa
cue: narrow depression located on the posterior scapula, superior to the spine

name: surgical neck
cue: region of the humerus where the expanded, proximal end joins with the narrower shaft

name: sustentaculum tali
cue: bony ledge extending from the medial side of the calcaneus bone

name: talus
cue: tarsal bone that articulates superiorly with the tibia and fibula at the ankle joint; also articulates inferiorly with the calcaneus bone and anteriorly with the navicular bone

name: tarsal bone
cue: one of the seven bones that make up the posterior foot; includes the calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuboid, medial cuneiform, intermediate cuneiform, and lateral cuneiform bones

name: thigh
cue: portion of the lower limb located between the hip and knee joints

name: tibia
cue: shin bone; the large, weight-bearing bone located on the medial side of the leg

name: tibial tuberosity
cue: elevated area on the anterior surface of the proximal tibia

name: trapezium
cue: from the lateral side, the first of the four distal carpal bones; articulates with the scaphoid proximally, the first and second metacarpals distally, and the trapezoid medially

name: trapezoid
cue: from the lateral side, the second of the four distal carpal bones; articulates with the scaphoid proximally, the second metacarpal distally, the trapezium laterally, and the capitate medially

name: triquetrum
cue: from the lateral side, the third of the four proximal carpal bones; articulates with the lunate laterally, the hamate distally, and has a facet for the pisiform

name: trochlea
cue: pulley-shaped region located medially at the distal end of the humerus; articulates at the elbow with the trochlear notch of the ulna

name: trochlear notch
cue: large, C-shaped depression located on the anterior side of the proximal ulna; articulates at the elbow with the trochlea of the humerus

name: ulna
cue: bone located on the medial side of the forearm

name: ulnar notch of the radius
cue: shallow, smooth area located on the medial side of the distal radius; articulates with the head of the ulna at the distal radioulnar joint

name: ulnar tuberosity
cue: roughened area located on the anterior, proximal ulna inferior to the coronoid process

name: abduction
cue: movement in the coronal plane that moves a limb laterally away from the body; spreading of the fingers

name: acetabular labrum
cue: lip of fibrocartilage that surrounds outer margin of the acetabulum on the hip bone

name: adduction
cue: movement in the coronal plane that moves a limb medially toward or across the midline of the body; bringing fingers together

name: amphiarthrosis
cue: slightly mobile joint

name: annular ligament
cue: intrinsic ligament of the elbow articular capsule that surrounds and supports the head of the radius at the proximal radioulnar joint

name: anterior cruciate ligament
cue: intracapsular ligament of the knee; extends from anterior, superior surface of the tibia to the inner aspect of the lateral condyle of the femur; resists hyperextension of knee

name: anterior talofibular ligament
cue: intrinsic ligament located on the lateral side of the ankle joint, between talus bone and lateral malleolus of fibula; supports talus at the talocrural joint and resists excess inversion of the foot

name: articular capsule
cue: connective tissue structure that encloses the joint cavity of a synovial joint

name: articular cartilage
cue: thin layer of hyaline cartilage that covers the articulating surfaces of bones at a synovial joint

name: articular disc
cue: meniscus; a fibrocartilage structure found between the bones of some synovial joints; provides padding or smooths movements between the bones; strongly unites the bones together

name: articulation
cue: joint of the body

name: atlanto-occipital joint
cue: articulation between the occipital condyles of the skull and the superior articular processes of the atlas (C1 vertebra)

name: atlantoaxial joint
cue: series of three articulations between the atlas (C1) vertebra and the axis (C2) vertebra, consisting of the joints between the inferior articular processes of C1 and the superior articular processes of C2, and the articulation between the dens of C2 and the anterior arch of C1

name: ball-and-socket joint
cue: synovial joint formed between the spherical end of one bone (the ball) that fits into the depression of a second bone (the socket); found at the hip and shoulder joints; functionally classified as a multiaxial joint

name: biaxial joint
cue: type of diarthrosis; a joint that allows for movements within two planes (two axes)

name: bursa
cue: connective tissue sac containing lubricating fluid that prevents friction between adjacent structures, such as skin and bone, tendons and bone, or between muscles

name: calcaneofibular ligament
cue: intrinsic ligament located on the lateral side of the ankle joint, between the calcaneus bone and lateral malleolus of the fibula; supports the talus bone at the ankle joint and resists excess inversion of the foot

name: cartilaginous joint
cue: joint at which the bones are united by hyaline cartilage (synchondrosis) or fibrocartilage (symphysis)

name: circumduction
cue: circular motion of the arm, thigh, hand, thumb, or finger that is produced by the sequential combination of flexion, abduction, extension, and adduction

name: condyloid joint
cue: synovial joint in which the shallow depression at the end of one bone receives a rounded end from a second bone or a rounded structure formed by two bones; found at the metacarpophalangeal joints of the fingers or the radiocarpal joint of the wrist; functionally classified as a biaxial joint

name: coracohumeral ligament
cue: intrinsic ligament of the shoulder joint; runs from the coracoid process of the scapula to the anterior humerus

name: deltoid ligament
cue: broad intrinsic ligament located on the medial side of the ankle joint; supports the talus at the talocrural joint and resists excess eversion of the foot

name: depression
cue: downward (inferior) motion of the scapula or mandible

name: diarthrosis
cue: freely mobile joint

name: dorsiflexion
cue: movement at the ankle that brings the top of the foot toward the anterior leg

name: elbow joint
cue: humeroulnar joint

name: elevation
cue: upward (superior) motion of the scapula or mandible

name: eversion
cue: foot movement involving the intertarsal joints of the foot in which the bottom of the foot is turned laterally, away from the midline

name: extension
cue: movement in the sagittal plane that increases the angle of a joint (straightens the joint); motion involving posterior bending of the vertebral column or returning to the upright position from a flexed position

name: extrinsic ligament
cue: ligament located outside of the articular capsule of a synovial joint

name: femoropatellar joint
cue: portion of the knee joint consisting of the articulation between the distal femur and the patella

name: fibrous joint
cue: joint where the articulating areas of the adjacent bones are connected by fibrous connective tissue

name: fibular collateral ligament
cue: extrinsic ligament of the knee joint that spans from the lateral epicondyle of the femur to the head of the fibula; resists hyperextension and rotation of the extended knee

name: flexion
cue: movement in the sagittal plane that decreases the angle of a joint (bends the joint); motion involving anterior bending of the vertebral column

name: fontanelles
cue: expanded areas of fibrous connective tissue that separate the braincase bones of the skull prior to birth and during the first year after birth

name: glenohumeral joint
cue: shoulder joint; articulation between the glenoid cavity of the scapula and head of the humerus; multiaxial ball-and-socket joint that allows for flexion/extension, abduction/adduction, circumduction, and medial/lateral rotation of the humerus

name: glenohumeral ligament
cue: one of the three intrinsic ligaments of the shoulder joint that strengthen the anterior articular capsule

name: glenoid labrum
cue: lip of fibrocartilage located around the outside margin of the glenoid cavity of the scapula

name: gomphosis
cue: type of fibrous joint in which the root of a tooth is anchored into its bony jaw socket by strong periodontal ligaments

name: hinge joint
cue: synovial joint at which the convex surface of one bone articulates with the concave surface of a second bone; includes the elbow, knee, ankle, and interphalangeal joints; functionally classified as a uniaxial joint

name: humeroradial joint
cue: articulation between the capitulum of the humerus and head of the radius

name: humeroulnar joint
cue: articulation between the trochlea of humerus and the trochlear notch of the ulna; uniaxial hinge joint that allows for flexion/extension of the forearm

name: hyperextension
cue: excessive extension of joint, beyond the normal range of movement

name: hyperflexion
cue: excessive flexion of joint, beyond the normal range of movement

name: iliofemoral ligament
cue: intrinsic ligament spanning from the ilium of the hip bone to the femur, on the superior-anterior aspect of the hip joint

name: inferior rotation
cue: movement of the scapula during upper limb adduction in which the glenoid cavity of the scapula moves in a downward direction as the medial end of the scapular spine moves in an upward direction

name: interosseous membrane
cue: wide sheet of fibrous connective tissue that fills the gap between two parallel bones, forming a syndesmosis; found between the radius and ulna of the forearm and between the tibia and fibula of the leg

name: intracapsular ligament
cue: ligament that is located within the articular capsule of a synovial joint

name: intrinsic ligament
cue: ligament that is fused to or incorporated into the wall of the articular capsule of a synovial joint

name: inversion
cue: foot movement involving the intertarsal joints of the foot in which the bottom of the foot is turned toward the midline

name: ischiofemoral ligament
cue: intrinsic ligament spanning from the ischium of the hip bone to the femur, on the posterior aspect of the hip joint

name: joint
cue: site at which two or more bones or bone and cartilage come together (articulate)

name: joint cavity
cue: space enclosed by the articular capsule of a synovial joint that is filled with synovial fluid and contains the articulating surfaces of the adjacent bones

name: joint interzone
cue: site within a growing embryonic limb bud that will become a synovial joint

name: lateral (external) rotation

name: lateral flexion

name: ligament of the head of the femur

name: medial (internal) rotation

name: medial excursion

name: medial meniscus
cue: C-shaped fibrocartilage articular disc located at the knee, between the medial condyle of the femur and medial condyle of the tibia

name: medial tibiofemoral joint
cue: portion of the knee consisting of the articulation between the medial condyle of the tibia and the medial condyle of the femur; allows for flexion/extension at the knee

name: meniscus
cue: articular disc

name: multiaxial joint
cue: type of diarthrosis; a joint that allows for movements within three planes (three axes)

name: opposition
cue: thumb movement that brings the tip of the thumb in contact with the tip of a finger

name: patellar ligament
cue: ligament spanning from the patella to the anterior tibia; serves as the final attachment for the quadriceps femoris muscle

name: periodontal ligament
cue: band of dense connective tissue that anchors the root of a tooth into the bony jaw socket

name: pivot joint
cue: synovial joint at which the rounded portion of a bone rotates within a ring formed by a ligament and an articulating bone; functionally classified as uniaxial joint

name: plane joint
cue: synovial joint formed between the flattened articulating surfaces of adjacent bones; functionally classified as a multiaxial joint

name: plantar flexion

name: pronated position

name: protraction

name: proximal radioulnar joint
cue: articulation between head of radius and radial notch of ulna; uniaxial pivot joint that allows for rotation of radius during pronation/ supination of forearm

name: pubofemoral ligament
cue: intrinsic ligament spanning from the pubis of the hip bone to the femur, on the anterior-inferior aspect of the hip joint

name: reposition
cue: movement of the thumb from opposition back to the anatomical position (next to index finger)

name: retraction
cue: posterior motion of the scapula or mandible

name: rotation

name: subacromial bursa
cue: bursa that protects the supraspinatus muscle tendon and superior end of the humerus from rubbing against the acromion of the scapula

name: subcutaneous bursa
cue: bursa that prevents friction between skin and an underlying bone

name: submuscular bursa
cue: bursa that prevents friction between bone and a muscle or between adjacent muscles

name: subscapular bursa
cue: bursa that prevents rubbing of the subscapularis muscle tendon against the scapula

name: subtalar joint
cue: articulation between the talus and calcaneus bones of the foot; allows motions that contribute to inversion/eversion of the foot

name: subtendinous bursa
cue: bursa that prevents friction between bone and a muscle tendon

name: superior rotation
cue: movement of the scapula during upper limb abduction in which the glenoid cavity of the scapula moves in an upward direction as the medial end of the scapular spine moves in a downward direction

name: supinated position
cue: forearm position in which the palm faces anteriorly (anatomical position)

name: supination
cue: forearm motion that moves the palm of the hand from the palm backward to the palm forward position

name: suture
cue: fibrous joint that connects the bones of the skull (except the mandible); an immobile joint (synarthrosis)

name: symphysis
cue: type of cartilaginous joint where the bones are joined by fibrocartilage

name: synarthrosis
cue: immobile or nearly immobile joint

name: synchondrosis
cue: type of cartilaginous joint where the bones are joined by hyaline cartilage

name: syndesmosis
cue: type of fibrous joint in which two separated, parallel bones are connected by an interosseous membrane

name: synostosis
cue: site at which adjacent bones or bony components have fused together

name: synovial fluid
cue: thick, lubricating fluid that fills the interior of a synovial joint

name: synovial joint
cue: joint at which the articulating surfaces of the bones are located within a joint cavity formed by an articular capsule

name: synovial membrane
cue: thin layer that lines the inner surface of the joint cavity at a synovial joint; produces the synovial fluid

name: talocrural joint

name: temporomandibular joint (TMJ)

name: tendon
cue: dense connective tissue structure that anchors a muscle to bone

name: tendon sheath
cue: connective tissue that surrounds a tendon at places where the tendon crosses a joint; contains a lubricating fluid to prevent friction and allow smooth movements of the tendon

name: tibial collateral ligament
cue: extrinsic ligament of knee joint that spans from the medial epicondyle of the femur to the medial tibia; resists hyperextension and rotation of extended knee

name: ulnar collateral ligament
cue: intrinsic ligament on the medial side of the elbow joint; spans from the medial epicondyle of the humerus to the medial ulna

name: uniaxial joint
cue: type of diarthrosis; joint that allows for motion within only one plane (one axis)

name: zygapophysial joints
cue: facet joints; plane joints between the superior and inferior articular processes of adjacent vertebrae that provide for only limited motions between the vertebrae

name: acetylcholine (ACh)
cue: neurotransmitter that binds at a motor end-plate to trigger depolarization

name: actin
cue: protein that makes up most of the thin myofilaments in a sarcomere muscle fiber

name: action potential
cue: change in voltage of a cell membrane in response to a stimulus that results in transmission of an electrical signal; unique to neurons and muscle fibers

name: aerobic respiration
cue: production of ATP in the presence of oxygen

name: angiogenesis
cue: formation of blood capillary networks

name: aponeurosis
cue: broad, tendon-like sheet of connective tissue that attaches a skeletal muscle to another skeletal muscle or to a bone

name: ATPase
cue: enzyme that hydrolyzes ATP to ADP

name: atrophy
cue: loss of structural proteins from muscle fibers

name: autorhythmicity
cue: heart’s ability to control its own contractions

name: calmodulin
cue: regulatory protein that facilitates contraction in smooth muscles

name: cardiac muscle
cue: striated muscle found in the heart; joined to one another at intercalated discs and under the regulation of pacemaker cells, which contract as one unit to pump blood through the circulatory system. Cardiac muscle is under involuntary control.

name: concentric contraction
cue: muscle contraction that shortens the muscle to move a load

name: contractility
cue: ability to shorten (contract) forcibly

name: contraction phase
cue: twitch contraction phase when tension increases

name: creatine phosphate
cue: phosphagen used to store energy from ATP and transfer it to muscle

name: dense body
cue: sarcoplasmic structure that attaches to the sarcolemma and shortens the muscle as thin filaments slide past thick filaments

name: depolarize
cue: to reduce the voltage difference between the inside and outside of a cell’s plasma membrane (the sarcolemma for a muscle fiber), making the inside less negative than at rest

name: desmosome
cue: cell structure that anchors the ends of cardiac muscle fibers to allow contraction to occur

name: eccentric contraction
cue: muscle contraction that lengthens the muscle as the tension is diminished

name: elasticity
cue: ability to stretch and rebound

name: endomysium
cue: loose, and well-hydrated connective tissue covering each muscle fiber in a skeletal muscle

name: epimysium
cue: outer layer of connective tissue around a skeletal muscle

name: excitability
cue: ability to undergo neural stimulation

name: excitation-contraction coupling
cue: sequence of events from motor neuron signaling to a skeletal muscle fiber to contraction of the fiber’s sarcomeres

name: extensibility
cue: ability to lengthen (extend)

name: fascicle
cue: bundle of muscle fibers within a skeletal muscle

name: fast glycolytic (FG)
cue: muscle fiber that primarily uses anaerobic glycolysis

name: fast oxidative (FO)
cue: intermediate muscle fiber that is between slow oxidative and fast glycolytic fibers

name: fibrosis
cue: replacement of muscle fibers by scar tissue

name: glycolysis
cue: anaerobic breakdown of glucose to ATP

name: graded muscle response
cue: modification of contraction strength

name: hyperplasia
cue: process in which one cell splits to produce new cells

name: hypertonia
cue: abnormally high muscle tone

name: hypertrophy
cue: addition of structural proteins to muscle fibers

name: hypotonia
cue: abnormally low muscle tone caused by the absence of low-level contractions

name: intercalated disc
cue: part of the sarcolemma that connects cardiac tissue, and contains gap junctions and desmosomes

name: isometric contraction
cue: muscle contraction that occurs with no change in muscle length

name: isotonic contraction
cue: muscle contraction that involves changes in muscle length

name: lactic acid
cue: product of anaerobic glycolysis

name: latch-bridges
cue: subset of a cross-bridge in which actin and myosin remain locked together

name: latent period
cue: the time when a twitch does not produce contraction

cue: sarcolemma of muscle fiber at the neuromuscular junction, with receptors for the neurotransmitter acetylcholine

name: motor unit
cue: motor neuron and the group of muscle fibers it innervates

name: muscle tension

name: muscle tone
cue: low levels of muscle contraction that occur when a muscle is not producing movement

name: myoblast
cue: muscle-forming stem cell

name: myofibril
cue: long, cylindrical organelle that runs parallel within the muscle fiber and contains the sarcomeres

name: myogram
cue: instrument used to measure twitch tension

name: myosin
cue: protein that makes up most of the thick cylindrical myofilament within a sarcomere muscle fiber

name: myotube
cue: fusion of many myoblast cells

name: neuromuscular junction (NMJ)
cue: synapse between the axon terminal of a motor neuron and the section of the membrane of a muscle fiber with receptors for the acetylcholine released by the terminal

name: neurotransmitter
cue: signaling chemical released by nerve terminals that bind to and activate receptors on target cells

name: oxygen debt
cue: amount of oxygen needed to compensate for ATP produced without oxygen during muscle contraction

name: pacesetter cell
cue: cell that triggers action potentials in smooth muscle

name: pericyte
cue: stem cell that regenerates smooth muscle cells

name: perimysium
cue: connective tissue that bundles skeletal muscle fibers into fascicles within a skeletal muscle

name: power stroke
cue: action of myosin pulling actin inward (toward the M line)

name: pyruvic acid
cue: product of glycolysis that can be used in aerobic respiration or converted to lactic acid

name: recruitment
cue: increase in the number of motor units involved in contraction

name: relaxation phase
cue: period after twitch contraction when tension decreases

name: sarcolemma
cue: plasma membrane of a skeletal muscle fiber

name: sarcomere
cue: longitudinally, repeating functional unit of skeletal muscle, with all of the contractile and associated proteins involved in contraction

name: sarcopenia
cue: age-related muscle atrophy

name: sarcoplasm
cue: cytoplasm of a muscle cell

name: sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR)
cue: specialized smooth endoplasmic reticulum, which stores, releases, and retrieves Ca++

name: satellite cell
cue: stem cell that helps to repair muscle cells

name: skeletal muscle
cue: striated, multinucleated muscle that requires signaling from the nervous system to trigger contraction; most skeletal muscles are referred to as voluntary muscles that move bones and produce movement

name: slow oxidative (SO)
cue: muscle fiber that primarily uses aerobic respiration

name: smooth muscle
cue: nonstriated, mononucleated muscle in the skin that is associated with hair follicles; assists in moving materials in the walls of internal organs, blood vessels, and internal passageways

name: somites
cue: blocks of paraxial mesoderm cells

name: stress-relaxation response
cue: relaxation of smooth muscle tissue after being stretched

name: synaptic cleft
cue: space between a nerve (axon) terminal and a motor end-plate

name: T-tubule
cue: projection of the sarcolemma into the interior of the cell

name: tetanus
cue: a continuous fused contraction

name: thick filament
cue: the thick myosin strands and their multiple heads projecting from the center of the sarcomere toward, but not all to way to, the Z-discs

name: thin filament
cue: thin strands of actin and its troponin- tropomyosin complex projecting from the Z-discs toward the center of the sarcomere

name: treppe
cue: stepwise increase in contraction tension

name: triad
cue: the grouping of one T-tubule and two terminal cisternae

name: tropomyosin
cue: regulatory protein that covers myosin- binding sites to prevent actin from binding to myosin

name: troponin
cue: regulatory protein that binds to actin, tropomyosin, and calcium

name: twitch
cue: single contraction produced by one action potential

name: varicosity
cue: enlargement of neurons that release neurotransmitters into synaptic clefts

name: visceral muscle
cue: smooth muscle found in the walls of visceral organs

name: voltage-gated sodium channels
cue: membrane proteins that open sodium channels in response to a sufficient voltage change, and initiate and transmit the action potential as Na+ enters through the channel

name: wave summation
cue: addition of successive neural stimuli to produce greater contraction
